title: test(types,app-shell): pin the metric-family single-measure refusal on every objectui dashboard-widget door (objectui#8894)
body:
Part of #8894
Clause-②: no

This PR lands the half of ruling D that survived measurement: the door pins. It deliberately does **not** remove `DatasetWidget`'s "Queried and then never displayed" warning, because the removal rests on a premise that measured false: the warning path is still reachable after the spec narrowing, on two arms. That half is returned to the PM seat as a decision (the `os-dev-report` on the card carries the options). The card stays open, so this body uses `Part of`.

## What lands

Tests and an empty-frontmatter changeset only; no source file moves.

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/dashboard-widget-metric-measure-door-8894.test.ts` pins two faces: `DashboardWidgetSchema` (the widget mirror) and `safeValidateSchema` (the published door, reached through a `dashboard` node's `widgets` slot; the CLI's `validate` command prints exactly this call's verdict).
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.metricMeasureArity-8894.test.ts` pins the third face: the metadata-admin editor's live validation (`validateMetadataDraft('dashboard', ...)`, which judges with the spec's own `DashboardSchema`), on both its `create` and `edit` doors.
- The metric family is **read off the spec's own rule at run time**, never written down: every member of the spec's `ChartTypeSchema` is put through the spec's `DashboardWidgetSchema` with two measures, and the types refused with a `custom` issue at `values` are the family. A non-vacuity check covers both directions (the family and its complement are each non-empty).
- A refusal is asserted as `code` + `path` + the spec's own message, read from the spec's parse of the same document; an acceptance is a full `safeParse` success. Controls: every other chart family keeps unbounded `values` (two measures plus a dimension parse on both doors), and a typeless widget is refused like a `metric` one, message included.

## Every objectui face that judges a dashboard widget, measured the same way

| face | two measures on a metric-family type | one measure |
|---|---|---|
| `DashboardWidgetSchema` (`@object-ui/types`) | refused, `custom` at `values`, the spec's message | parses |
| `safeValidateSchema` / CLI `validate` (`@object-ui/types`) | refused, `custom` at `widgets.0.values` | parses |
| `validateMetadataDraft('dashboard')`, create and edit doors (`@object-ui/app-shell`) | refused at `widgets.0.values` | `ok: true` |
| `validateTree` (`@object-ui/sdui-parser`) | silent | silent |
| TypeScript `DashboardWidgetSchema['values']` | `string[]`, as on the spec's own inferred type | |

No face that judges widget shape accepts two measures on the family, so nothing is narrowed here. `validateTree` is listed because it does read dashboard widgets, but it is not a widget-shape door: it is equally silent on `values: 42` and on an unknown widget key, and its lit control (an unconsumed `options.invert` on a gauge) does draw its `unconsumed-widget-option` warning. The TypeScript face is out of scope by the card's ruling.

## Why the warning is not removed

The ruling's consequence was "the caption path becomes unreachable and is removed", and the claim's reason for `Clause-②: no` was "this card removes a warning no accepted document reaches". Both measured false at `d0ae5d025` with `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 installed:

1. **The dimensionless arm is door-accepted and still reaches the warning.** `DatasetWidget` classifies a tile as `METRIC_TYPES.has(type) || dimensions.length === 0`, and the spec's arity rule reads `type` only. A `bar`, `pie` or `table` widget with no `dimensions` and two or more measures is ACCEPTED by the spec's `DashboardWidgetSchema`, by objectui's mirror, by `safeValidateSchema` and by the metadata-admin client validation. Rendered, `{ type: 'table', dataset: 'sales', values: ['revenue', 'cost', 'margin'] }` produces a single-number tile showing `revenue` only, and the warning fires naming `cost` and `margin`. The existing pin "SUBJECT: covers the dimensionless arm, where any widget type becomes a tile" in `DatasetWidget.unrenderedMeasures-8894.test.tsx` exercises exactly this path and is green on `main`. ⚠️ The spec's own refusal text (and its ADR-0087 entry) tells an author who hits the metric refusal that "`type: 'table'` renders a row of measures"; an author who switches the type and adds no dimension lands on this arm.
2. **Stored rows reach the renderer unconverted.** The installed spec's ADR-0087 entry `dashboard-widget-metric-family-multi-measure-refused` is a static semantic migration, not a conversion; its own text says "The migration does not do this for you and no conversion could". On the server side (objectstack `288611e3e`), the metadata read path only decorates a stored document with `_diagnostics` and never refuses it (`computeMetadataDiagnostics`, and the note in `metadata-type-schemas.ts` that begins "Nothing re-parses stored rows through this registry"). So a dashboard saved before 17.5.0 with three measures on a `metric` tile is served as stored, and `DatasetWidget` renders `values[0]`. The `_diagnostics` badge reaches Studio's directory views; no `_diagnostics` reader sits on the dashboard view.

Removing the warning would re-silence both arms, and on arm 1 nothing else speaks: the doors are green and `_diagnostics` reads `valid: true`. That is the silence ruling D was made to end, so the removal waits for a decision instead of being forced onto a dead premise.

Untouched and still green: `DatasetWidget.tsx`, its warning pin file, and objectui#8887's two pins in `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx` (the byte-identical sub-caption-less tile, and "those measures are still dropped").

## Verification (all at `ff0f926d4` unless marked)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the two new pins, `spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts`, `DatasetWidget.unrenderedMeasures-8894.test.tsx` and `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`: `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 99 passed (99)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (the markdown ledger and doc-version ratchet live there): `Test Files 177 passed | 2 skipped (179)`, `Tests 5371 passed | 2 skipped (5373)`. `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` exits 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` exits 0 (run on the same test bytes before the commit; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin). `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exits 0 after building its dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`, 28 of 28 tasks); `--listFilesOnly` lists the new app-shell pin.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both new test files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-control-bytes.mjs`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` (0 new citations), `check-test-path-roots.mjs`, `check-changeset-claims.mjs`, `check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs`, `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.

**Ablation (the door pin can fail).** From committed `ff0f926d4`, `.superRefine(checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity);` in `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts` was replaced by a `void` of the same identifier (one anchor asserted before writing). On disk: anchor count 0, marker count 1, blob `da1964cf` became `81f1b65c`. Result: `Tests 11 failed | 31 passed (42)`, exactly the eleven refusal cases red by name (five face-1 types, the typeless case, five face-2 types) and every acceptance, control and derivation case green. Restored by `git checkout HEAD --` with the blob back to `da1964cf` and `git diff HEAD` empty, under a trap on EXIT INT TERM with absolute paths. No `dist/` is involved: the pin imports `../zod/complex.zod` relatively.

## Acceptance notes

- The stale sentence "`values` is `z.array(z.string()).min(1)` on `DashboardWidgetSchema`, so an author may legally declare three measures" sits in the warning's comment block in `DatasetWidget.tsx` and in its pin file's header; since 17.5.0 it is false for the metric family and true for the dimensionless arm. It is left for the follow-up that settles the warning, which edits both files anyway.
- The warning's own advice ("use a widget that renders every measure (table, pivot or a chart)") is wrong on the dimensionless arm, where a `table` without a dimension is itself the tile.
- The spec's 17.5.0 CHANGELOG entry and its schema docblock attribute a "not rendered" sub-caption to objectui PR #8887; that PR landed the declared-description sub-caption, and the drop signal is PR #8905's console warning. Ruling D's phrase "caption path" inherits the same reading. Carrier: none.
